description: Current image-defect and missing-letter apparatus for the proposed solution.
coordinates: Top-left pixel origin. bbox_ltrb is [left, top, right, bottom]; left/top inclusive, right/bottom exclusive.
addresses: Row and token positions are 1-based in revised_tokens.txt. source_units identifies existing signs. For gaps these are neighboring signs, not missing cipher units.
edited_letters: Letters used by the editorial reading at the site; they do not change the canonical token stream or key. At the two blotted sites the proposed literal letters already equal the edited letters.
comparison_labels_by_letter: Final cipher labels with the stated single-letter key value, provided for comparison; this is not a claim that those glyphs occur at the defect site.
scope: 17 sites comprise 13 existing-unit sites spanning 14 class-C units, plus four gaps. Origin assessments are undecidable; favored explanations are hypotheses.
resolution_limit: The available cipher detail is 1051 x 1246 pixels, reproduced from a 1202 x 1836 page. Individual signs span only tens of pixels. Fine lost or merged strokes, original ink and reproduction loss cannot be distinguished conclusively; an independent manuscript witness has not established the origin of these anomalies.

sites.visual_finding: g-like bowl and returned descender agree with other g units. No R-label family gives a closer supported reading.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the visible S-valued form; its origin remains undecidable. Literal S is retained.

sites.visual_finding: No separately bounded extra glyph is visible between A and 55. Both A exemplars have the same basic crossbar; no T can be split off on the available pixels.
sites.interpretation: An omission is possible; no additional cipher unit is supported. T is supplied only in the editorial reading.

sites.visual_finding: The row meets the reproduced right edge. No separate E appears before the next row begins with P; the image cannot establish whether a mark was lost at the edge.
sites.interpretation: Reproduction clipping and an original omission both remain possible. E is supplied only in the editorial reading.

sites.visual_finding: The digits read 79: compare the closed lower 9 and the 76 exemplars. Replacing 79 globally with S would damage the other 28 occurrences.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the visible R-valued form; its origin remains undecidable. Literal R is retained.

sites.visual_finding: Short ascender and right bowl match b. The needed E families have a fork, staff, crossed stroke, numeral, A or circular stem; none supports a local relabel.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the visible I-valued form; its origin remains undecidable. Literal I is retained.

sites.visual_finding: The final sign is m-shaped like the six other m occurrences. No separate E/D/T units can be segmented here. Expanding it to EDT would be a positional exception.
sites.interpretation: Historical name spelling or an enciphering error may explain the mismatch. Literal F is retained; EDT is an editorial name restoration.

sites.visual_finding: No separate triangle or numeral 17 is visible between CURLD and 79. A merged Y is not demonstrated. Inserting Y is a name restoration; omission versus a spelling variant is not settled by this witness.
sites.interpretation: The conventional name restoration does not prove an original defect. Y is supplied only in the editorial reading.

sites.visual_finding: The nearly straight descending stem falls within variation among q exemplars. No diagnostic g return is resolved; a faint g curl lost in reproduction cannot be excluded.
sites.interpretation: q/T is the working transcription. The historical glyph identity and the cause of the mismatch remain unresolved. HOMMET is literal; HOMMES is editorial.

sites.visual_finding: The sign is faint but has a g-like return. Loss of a small distinguishing detail versus an A-family sign cannot be excluded at native resolution.
sites.interpretation: A g/S form and a damaged A-valued form remain possible. Literal S is retained; A is editorial.

sites.visual_finding: Loop with descending right stem falls within q exemplars. The question-mark, phi, dotted-cross and 82 families for U are visually different.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the visible T-valued form; its origin remains undecidable. Literal T is retained.

sites.visual_finding: Two units are visible: q followed by +. Both have repeated exemplars. Neither a hidden S/O unit nor a supported alternate segmentation is visible.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the two visible forms; its origin remains undecidable. Literal T + DE is retained; SO is editorial.

sites.visual_finding: Tall crossed stem and lower hook match JCROSS. No needed-T label is visibly established at this position.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the visible R-valued form; its origin remains undecidable. Literal R is retained.

sites.visual_finding: Short upper bar and low curve match OVERLINEARC, including other low and flattened exemplars. Neither a colon nor g/76-like S form is supported.
sites.interpretation: An enciphering substitution is favored by the visible R-valued form; its origin remains undecidable. Literal R is retained.

sites.visual_finding: Faint rounded form with an upper curl is compatible with d; comparison with o/STEMCIRCLE and the other E families does not resolve the fine contour.
sites.interpretation: A d/A form and a damaged E-valued form remain possible. Literal A is retained; E is editorial.

sites.visual_finding: The DIV and following 42 are individually visible; no additional TI pair or merged T form is resolved in the gap. An inserted TI would add plaintext without image-supported units.
sites.interpretation: An omission is possible; no additional cipher unit is supported. TI is supplied only in the editorial reading.

sites.visual_finding: A heavy crossing blot obscures the central sign. The long dark descender prevents a secure identity with ordinary x exemplars. N is retained as a proposal, not promoted through the x family.
sites.interpretation: The original ink or reproduction defect and the glyph identity are unresolved. N remains a proposed key value.

sites.visual_finding: Triangular upper contour and rounded bowl are visible, but the dark interior obscures the stroke structure. Resemblance to THETA does not authenticate the C value.
sites.interpretation: The original ink or reproduction defect and the glyph identity are unresolved. C remains a proposed key value.
